chunks: From him, from Fadalah, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abu al-Jarud, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
"If you sell [an item] to a man on condition, then if he brings you your money, [the sale is valid]; otherwise, the sale is for you [i.e., you may keep the item or the sale stands as yours]."

key_terms.فَالْبَيْعُ لَكَ: then the sale is for you

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a conditional sale in Shia jurisprudence if the condition is not met?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* within the chapter on sales contracts, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the legal status of conditional sales (*al-bay' 'ala shart*). It establishes that if the buyer fulfills the stipulated condition, the transaction is finalized; however, if they fail to do so, the phrase 'the sale is yours' (*al-bay' laka*) is interpreted by Shia jurists to mean the seller retains the right to reclaim the item or the contract remains voidable, protecting the seller from loss.
